name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Hormuz crossings fell over 40% to 125 ships on 17–23 Nov; Houthis claim attacks on Saudi Red Sea ports 25 Nov
state: Marine Traffic data show 125 vessels crossed Hormuz on 17–23 Nov against 226 on 1–7 Nov, a fall of more than 40%, and 28 crossed in the 24 hours to 24 Nov against 125–140 a day before the war (Al Jazeera). UKMTO said two tankers were hit in the strait on 22 Nov (Gulf News). On 25 Nov the Houthis claimed attacks on the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, and the coalition said a projectile hit Jazan, causing minor damage (Middle East Eye).
for_you: Shipping disruption raises freight costs and delivery times. Seafarers and operators should follow UKMTO and JMIC advisories.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded (>40% fall in transits) = Alert

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Hormuz oil traffic is down 40 percent: are Iran's tanker attacks working?
Gulf News — Bahrain intercepts Iranian attacks as Tehran prepares 14 oil tankers to breach US naval blockade
Middle East Eye — Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
